Chuyen Nho read-aloud tool - third-party software and data

Voice model: Piper vi_VN-vais1000-medium (rhasspy/piper-voices)
File: vi_VN-vais1000-medium-ec7c89e2.onnx
SHA-256: ec7c89e2c85f4d1edc24b6120c18aaf1bda614f06b511567eb9c7c0de15e2dab
Source: https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices/tree/main/vi/vi_VN/vais1000/medium
Training data: VAIS-1000 Vietnamese Speech Synthesis Corpus, licensed CC BY 4.0
https://ieee-dataport.org/documents/vais-1000-vietnamese-speech-synthesis-corpus
https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
Model card: MODEL_CARD-vais1000 (in this directory). The card states the voice was fine-tuned
from the U.S. English "lessac" Piper voice; see docs/read-aloud-tts.md for the open licensing review.
Piper (architecture and training code): https://github.com/rhasspy/piper, MIT.

Phonemizer: @diffusionstudio/piper-wasm 1.0.0 (npm, declared MIT)
Files: piper-phonemize-1.0.0/piper_phonemize.wasm, piper-phonemize-1.0.0/piper_phonemize.data
The WebAssembly build links piper-phonemize (MIT) with eSpeak NG and embeds its language data.
eSpeak NG is GPL-3.0-or-later; license: COPYING.GPLv3 (in this directory).
Build recipe: https://github.com/diffusion-studio/piper-wasm (README, June 2024)
Sources: https://github.com/rhasspy/espeak-ng and https://github.com/wide-video/piper-phonemize
The upstream recipe clones both repositories at their default branch without a pinned commit, so it
is not evidence that a rebuild reproduces the published binary byte-for-byte.

ONNX Runtime Web 1.30.0 (MIT) is shared with the background-removal tool; see
../background-removal/LICENSE-ONNXRUNTIME.

Assets are served unchanged; scripts/prepare-tts.mjs verifies their SHA-256 checksums.
This notice accompanies the third-party assets and does not replace their licenses.
